name: Modest Mouse
label: Matador
lede: Isaac Brock built Modest Mouse out of Issaquah strip malls, a video-store friendship and a drummer found at a metal show. The band made the Northwest's most restless records, then picked up a Smith, a platinum hit and three decades of trouble.

eras.title: Issaquah, on purpose
eras.text: Brock kept the band in Issaquah, a suburb east of Seattle, on purpose: not Seattle, not Olympia, just strip malls and cul-de-sacs to write about. Calvin Johnson's Olympia orbit put out the first records, and Up Records took over from there.

years.src: Wikipedia: Modest Mouse · Wikipedia: Isaac Brock
years.h: Two teenagers meet in a video store and find a drummer at a metal show
years.p: Isaac Brock and bassist Eric Judy meet as teenagers outside Seattle; drummer Jeremiah Green turns up at a heavy metal show. That's Modest Mouse.
years.xp:
Brock was born in Helena, Montana, and moved to Issaquah at 11. He was raised in Grace Gospel Church and, by Wikipedia's account, was asked to speak in tongues at age six. Religion runs through the songs.

The band name comes from a line in Virginia Woolf's short story The Mark on the Wall about modest, mouse-coloured people. It has nothing to do with the composer Modest Mussorgsky, whatever the jokes say.

years.h: Calvin Johnson's Olympia studio hosts the first EP
years.p: Blue Cadet-3, Do You Connect? comes out on K Records, cut at Dub Narcotic Studio with John Wickhart on bass and Dann Gallucci on guitar.

years.h: Sad Sappy Sucker sits on the shelf for seven years
years.p: Recorded in 1994 as the band's first album for K Records, it runs into delay after delay and is forgotten. K finally releases it in 2001.

years.cap: Isaac Brock, Eric Judy and Jeremiah Green, c. 1996
years.h: Steve Wold records the debut, years before he becomes Seasick Steve
years.p: This Is a Long Drive for Someone with Nothing to Think About is cut at Moon Studios in Olympia and released by Up Records. The Interstate 8 EP follows the same year.
play: This Is a Long Drive for Someone with Nothing to Think About

eras.title: Highways, malls and bad religion
eras.text: The Lonesome Crowded West sold steadily without a hit and turned a small band into a cause. The majors started calling.

q: The Lonesome Crowded West is the greatest Northwest record ever made.
yt: Full set from the master, Knoxville, September 9, 1997
years.h: The Lonesome Crowded West gets an 8.9, then a 10 seventeen years later
years.p: Recorded May 22 to June 7, 1997, at Moon Studios in Olympia with Calvin Johnson and Scott Swayze. Pitchfork upgraded its 8.9 to a 10 in 2014.
years.xp:
Phil Ek recorded three tracks in Seattle. By June 2000, per Nielsen SoundScan figures, it had sold over 60,000 copies in the US with no radio single.

In 2014 Brock's own label, Glacial Pace, put it back on vinyl in its original two-cover package.

years.h: Cleveland gets Modest Mouse in a DIY punk space
years.p: Speak in Tongues was one of the rooms the band kept booking long after it could have filled bigger ones.

years.h: Brock's jaw is broken mid-album and wired shut
years.p: Five months into recording The Moon & Antarctica at Clava Studios in Chicago, Brock is attacked near the band's lodging.
years.xp:
Producer [[Brian Deck|e91d5dc5-12a7-45cf-af2b-f120def0f711]] of [[Califone|68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda]] says Brock spent a week in hospital and had his jaw wired for two or three months. The studio wasn't even finished when the band arrived.

Deck and Brock had met on a shared bill at the Magic Stick in Detroit, where they hung out until the end of the night.

eras.title: Epic signs on, the drummer walks
eras.text: The first major-label record was bleaker and stranger than anything before it, and critics loved it. A car commercial and a festival package tour followed, and in 2003 the founding drummer left.

years.h: Pitchfork's third-best album of 2000 is on Epic
years.p: The Moon & Antarctica, the major-label debut, gets a 9.8. Up Records puts out the rarities set Building Nothing Out of Something the same year.
years.xp: Producer [[Brian Deck|e91d5dc5-12a7-45cf-af2b-f120def0f711]] and the band spent five months on the record in Chicago, a stretch that included Brock's broken jaw.

years.big: …can bitch about my principles while they spend their parents' money
years.h: Gravity Rides Everything goes into a Nissan Quest ad
years.p: Modest Mouse licenses the song from The Moon & Antarctica to a Nissan minivan commercial. The line above is Isaac Brock's answer to fans who objected.
years.xp: Brock didn't pretend otherwise: he called the deal commercial, and necessary. He said the money kept the band alive and aimed his answer at fans with trust funds and dish-washing jobs.

years.h: Modest Mouse rides the Unlimited Sunshine Tour with Cake and De La Soul
years.p: The package bill also carries [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]], the Hackensaw Boys and Kinky. Brock releases Sharpen Your Teeth as [[Ugly Casanova|5c2d7596-2366-47c5-b4a2-0550ac8f9e69]] the same year.

years.h: Green quits on his 26th birthday
years.p: Jeremiah Green leaves after a breakdown; the official line is that he's off to his side band Vells. [[Helio Sequence|b6ab8d01-0cb3-4515-bc05-d928397e7429]] drummer Benjamin Weikel and returning guitarist Dann Gallucci step in.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports that Green had been hospitalized and diagnosed with bipolar disorder, and that he had severe manic episodes when medication was mixed with alcohol and mushrooms. He came back briefly, then disappeared for two months during recording sessions in Portland.

eras.title: Float On, everywhere
eras.text: The record made without Green became the one everybody knew. A public radio show, late-night TV and two Grammy nominations took a band that once played Cleveland basements to platinum.

years.h: Marketplace uses Float On as bumper music
years.p: Good News for People Who Love Bad News comes out with Float On and Ocean Breathes Salty as its hits, and is later certified platinum.
play: Good News for People Who Love Bad News

years.h: Green is back behind the kit a month after Good News
years.p: Jeremiah Green returns in May. Benjamin Weikel goes back to [[Helio Sequence|b6ab8d01-0cb3-4515-bc05-d928397e7429]] full time.

years.h: An avalanche on Mount Rainier kills Brock's adopted brother
years.p: Isaac Brock's adopted brother, Ansel Vizcaya, dies on the mountain.

years.h: Brock's day job at Sub Pop lands Wolf Parade
years.p: Working on Sub Pop's A&R team, Isaac Brock signs Montreal's [[Wolf Parade|b7ddce8b-9e5c-46bd-9d33-41b134ce1a7f]].

years.h: Saturday Night Live gets both hits
years.p: Modest Mouse plays Float On and Ocean Breathes Salty. Good News is nominated for Best Alternative Album, and Float On for Best Rock Song.

eras.title: A Smith joins the band
eras.text: Johnny Marr of The Smiths signed on as a full member and the next record went straight to No. 1. Then Marr left, and in 2012 so did Eric Judy, the last founder besides Brock and Green.

years.cap: Modest Mouse on stage, spring 2007, the Marr line-up
years.h: Johnny Marr takes Gallucci's spot as a full member
years.p: Dann Gallucci leaves on good terms and Marr, formerly of [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]], joins as a member, not a hired gun.

years.h: Florida's Bang festival cuts the set short
years.p: After the Bang Music Festival in November, Modest Mouse stays out of Miami, Orlando and St. Augustine until June 2008.

years.h: We Were Dead Before the Ship Even Sank gives the band its first No. 1
years.p: Delayed from December 2006, it tops the Billboard 200 and throws off Dashboard, Missed the Boat and We've Got Everything.
play: We Were Dead Before the Ship Even Sank

years.h: Heath Ledger starts a King Rat video and doesn't finish it
years.p: Ledger loved the song before its release and began a video with his collective The Masses. He died in January 2008.

years.h: Marr heads to The Cribs and Jim Fairchild takes the guitar
years.p: Johnny Marr joins [[The Cribs|a3a92047-be1c-4f3e-8960-c4f8570984df]]. No One's First, and You're Next, an EP of leftovers, follows on August 4.

years.h: Founding bassist Eric Judy leaves after nearly two decades
years.p: Russell Higbee of [[Man Man|4e210d41-b3e3-4e34-8c3b-3b8cc2116562]] takes bass. Pitchfork.tv also airs a 45-minute film on The Lonesome Crowded West.

eras.title: Glacial pace
eras.text: Eight years passed between albums. Brock took back his old records on his own label, Glacial Pace, and the band returned with violins and extra percussion.

years.h: Brock puts the first two albums back out on his own label
years.p: Glacial Pace reissues This Is a Long Drive... and The Lonesome Crowded West on CD and vinyl.

years.h: Eight years later, Strangers to Ourselves
years.p: The first album since 2007 is preceded by Lampshades on Fire, which debuts on Minnesota public station 89.3 The Current.
years.xp: Lampshades on Fire first aired on 89.3 The Current on December 15, 2014, a little under three months before the album.

years.h: Musixmatch counts a swear word every 310 words
years.p: Its analysis of 43,414 songs ranks Modest Mouse second among indie rock bands, behind only The Neighbourhood.

years.cap: Modest Mouse live in Pittsburgh, August 2021
years.h: Jeremiah Green plays on his last album, The Golden Casket
years.p: The seventh album gets a mixed read from the Wall Street Journal, which called the first half overstuffed and praised the stripped-down closer Back to the Middle.

eras.title: Losing Jeremiah
eras.text: A 25th-anniversary tour for The Lonesome Crowded West ended with the death of the drummer who played on it. Brock kept going: the 2004 line-up for a victory lap, then an eighth album with new players.

years.cap: Modest Mouse at Shaky Knees, Atlanta
years.h: Jeremiah Green dies at 45
years.p: Green took unannounced leave from the Lonesome Crowded West 25th-anniversary tour. His stage IV cancer was made public on December 25, and he died in Sequim, Washington, six days later.
years.xp: Green played on every Modest Mouse album but one, from the first EP to The Golden Casket. Stylus Magazine had ranked him 37th among the greatest rock drummers.

years.h: Weikel returns for a Good News anniversary tour
years.p: Benjamin Weikel, who drummed on the record, rejoins Isaac Brock. Eric Judy, Dann Gallucci and Tom Peloso do not. That summer Modest Mouse co-headlines with [[Pixies|b6b2bb8d-54a9-491f-9607-7b546023b433]].

years.h: An Eraser and a Maze brings in three new players
years.p: The eighth album, and the first in five years, adds Simon O'Connor, Damon Cox and Keith Karman. Brock says a Golden Casket companion, Shadows in the Shade, is due around 2027.
years.xp: Brock has said Shadows in the Shade will feature Johnny Marr on Rivers of Rivers and posthumous contributions from Jeremiah Green.
